text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE TIMES - Growing concern over "buy now, pay later" culture. Plastic money seen practical by some, devil in disguise by others.

- Thomas De La Rue manufacturing director for Malta talks. Mr Roy Allen is due in Malta next week to discuss the future of the Malta plant of the international security printing firm following a slump in work orders. Workers at the plant are currently working a four day week.

L-ORIZZONT - Malta Drydocks to pay compensation to explosion victims on Monday. The compensation sparked off protests against the dockyard's management last week but the council then agreed with the demands by the relatives of the nine workers killed in an explosion two years ago.

IN-NAZZJON - Opposition proposes law on drugs. Tonio Borg, shadow minister for home affairs said Parliament should debate and approve a draft law prepared by the former Nationalist government but never debated in parliament because of the elections. The bill would increase jail terms for those found trafficking in psychotropic drugs. Borg said there was currently an anomaly in that those trafficking narcotic drugs, such as hashish, could be jailed for life, and those trafficking psychotropic drugs like ecstasy were only liable for 20 years behind bars.
